body:
- **Example Screener queries (written by this researcher in Screener's syntax; field names match Screener's standard ratio names but should be pasted and tested before use):**
  - *Quality compounder:* `Market Capitalization > 2000 AND Average return on capital employed 5Years > 20 AND Return on equity > 18 AND Debt to equity < 0.3 AND Sales growth 5Years > 12 AND Profit growth 5Years > 12 AND Pledged percentage < 5 AND Promoter holding > 40`
  - *GARP:* `Profit growth 3Years > 20 AND Sales growth 3Years > 15 AND Return on capital employed > 18 AND PEG Ratio < 1.2 AND Price to Earning < Industry PE AND Debt to equity < 0.5 AND Market Capitalization > 1000`
  - *Turnaround:* `Net profit > 0 AND Net Profit last year < 0 AND Sales growth > 20 AND OPM > OPM last year AND Debt to equity < 1 AND Pledged percentage < 10` (Screener also supports quarterly fields like `Net Profit latest quarter`, `Net Profit preceding year quarter`, `YOY Quarterly sales growth`).
  - *Small-cap multibagger hunt:* `Market Capitalization > 300 AND Market Capitalization < 5000 AND Sales growth 3Years > 20 AND Profit growth 3Years > 25 AND Return on capital employed > 18 AND Debt to equity < 0.5 AND Promoter holding > 50 AND Pledged percentage = 0 AND Cash from operations last year > 0`
  - *Forensic overlay to add to any screen:* `AND Cash from operations 5Years > 0.7 * Net profit 5Years` (approximating cumulative CFO/PAT; check exact field names for cumulative CFO), `AND Debtor days < 90`, `AND Pledged percentage < 5`.
- **Role of each tool [BACKGROUND, not re-verified this session]:** Trendlyne – DVM scores, insider/SAST/bulk-block deal trackers, superstar portfolio tracker, MF holdings changes; Tijori Finance – segment/operational KPIs (capacity, volumes, store counts) and concall summaries; Tickertape – screener + MF/ETF data; Chartink – technical scanners (breakouts, volume); BSE/NSE "Corporate Announcements" – results, concall transcripts, investor presentations, credit-rating intimations, SAST Reg 29 and PIT Reg 7 disclosures, pledge (Reg 31) filings; NSE/BSE bulk & block deal pages; AMFI/AMC monthly portfolio disclosures for MF holdings; CRISIL/ICRA/CARE/India Ratings rationale PDFs (liquidity, contingent liabilities, group support, "Issuer Not Cooperating" status); Valuepickr – long-form stock threads with annual report notes and concall summaries.
- The Kaynes case shows a cheap retail check: compare related-party disclosures across the listed parent, subsidiaries and the promoter's private entities (MCA filings) — mismatches are a signal even when they turn out to be disclosure errors.

`case_study:constellation-software-2006-2026` · tickers CA-CSU · confidence: verified

Founded 1995 by ex-VC Mark Leonard; IPO on TSX May 2006 (~C$17.50 [unverified]). Model: buy hundreds of small vertical-market software (VMS) firms at low multiples with strict hurdle rates, keep them decentralised, reinvest all cash flow; Leonard's letters reported ROIC and organic growth candidly and set the playbook (later spun-offs Topicus, Lumine). Peak ~C$5,000-5,300 (2025) [unverified] ≈ 300x + dividends. Split: almost entirely FCF/share growth; P/E/FCF multiple also rose from ~10-15x to ~30x+ [approx]. Drawdowns: ~-35-40% in 2008 [unverified]; then the big one: Sept 25 2025 Leonard resigned for health reasons (Mark Miller president), shares closed the week -17% days after an investor call on AI worries; National Bank downgraded; AI-disruption fear hit all SaaS/VMS; by Feb 2026 ~-51% from highs, 52-week low ~C$2,624 (Jan 2026), ~16-17x forward earnings by mid-2026. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2006-2012: shareholder letters showing high returns on many small, boring acquisitions, a growing count of deals per year, and owner-operator incentives (managers required to buy shares with bonus). Who caught it: early backers OMERS/Ontario pension funds; a cult following of quality investors [names unverified]. LESSON: capital-allocation compounders depend on the allocator and on the redeployment runway; key-person exit + a new technology threat can halve even a 300x stock without any fundamental miss yet.

- **Start → end:** ~C$17.50 IPO [unverified] → ~C$5,000+ peak (2025) [unverified]; ~C$2,600 low Jan 2026 (~300x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** mostly FCF/share; some rerating
- **Max drawdown:** ~-51% (2025-26)
- **Early signal:** letters showing high ROIC on small VMS deals; owner incentives
- **Who caught it:** pension backers; quality-investor following [unverified]
- **Ended/stalled:** Sept 2025 founder exit + AI fears
- **Lesson:** key-person + runway risk in serial acquirers
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-09-25/constellation-software-falls-as-founder-mark-leonard-resigns) · [2](https://betakit.com/constellation-software-shares-close-week-down-17-percent-after-founder-and-ceo-steps-down/) · [3](https://thelogic.co/briefing/constellation-software-founder-steps-down-citing-health-reasons/) · [4](https://nai500.com/blog/2026/02/constellation-software-plunges-51-sparking-debate-on-ai-fear-and-value/) · [5](https://ts2.tech/en/constellation-softwares-48-slide-has-investors-split-as-ai-fears-rattle-software-stocks/)

`person:group-vedanta` · flag: **mixed** · confidence: single-source · tickers: VEDL, HINDZINC

Flag: MIXED (leaning poor on minority treatment). UK-based Vedanta Resources (VRL, promoter holdco) carries large debt serviced largely by dividends and brand fees from listed Vedanta Ltd (VEDL), which in turn controls Hindustan Zinc (~61%). Pattern: very high dividend payouts upstream (good for VEDL minorities' cash yield but driven by holdco debt needs), plus brand and strategic-service fees -- Viceroy Research (Jul-2025) alleged VEDL and subsidiaries paid ~$361 m (Rs 3,085 cr) in brand fees to VRL in FY25 and called the structure a 'parasite' holdco; Vedanta rejected the report as 'selective misinformation'. A shareholder PIL on brand fees was reported (undated). History of contested minority actions: Cairn India merger (2017) with preference-share consideration; failed delisting of Vedanta Ltd (2020) when promoters sought to buy out minorities near lows; Vedanta lending to/receiving from group entities; Sterlite Copper Tuticorin closure (2018, after police firing on protesters). Hindustan Zinc's government (~28%) stake gives some check on cash moves. Status Nov-2026: VEDL's demerger into Vedanta Aluminium, Oil & Gas, Power, Iron & Steel plus residual Vedanta Ltd (with HZL) became effective 1-May-2026 (record date, 1:1 shares); VEDL revised dividend policy to drop mandatory HZL dividend up-streaming; lost Jaiprakash Associates to Adani at NCLAT (May-2026). Watch: brand-fee agreements at each demerged entity, ICDs to VRL, promoter pledges (historically ~99% of VEDL promoter shares encumbered -- verify current SAST). (Tickers of the four demerged entities were not verified here; check NSE.)

- **allegations:** Viceroy Jul-2025 (denied, no regulator finding)
- **red flags:** brand fees to holdco; holdco debt dependence; 2020 delisting attempt at lows; high encumbrance
- **good conduct:** high dividends; demerger with 1:1 mirror shares

body:
`insight:marks-bubble-com-2000` | confidence: verified | date: 2000-01-02

Memo of 2 Jan 2000, Marks's first widely read memo, written after reading Edward Chancellor's 'Devil Take the Hindmost'. Uses the 1720 South Sea Bubble as a template: companies financed losses by issuing stock at ever-higher prices; 'Some argued that the higher the shares rose, the more they were actually worth' - Marks's gloss: '[There's no such thing as too high a price if the concept is right...]'; the legendary company 'for carrying on an undertaking of great advantage but no one to know what it is' - gloss: '[I can't understand what it does, but that's okay]'. Isaac Newton sold early, bought back at the top and lost £20,000. RCA fell from $114 to $2.5 within three years after 1929; airlines' cumulative profit from founding to 1992 was zero despite transforming the world. Verdict quoted in his 2023 recap: 'I find the evidence of an overheated, speculative market in technology, Internet and telecommunications stocks overwhelming, as are the similarities to past manias.' Outcome (per 'Taking the Temperature', 2023): S&P 500 -46% from 2000 high to 2002 low, NASDAQ -80%. Marks's definition: a bubble is 'an irrationally elevated opinion of an asset or sector.' Markers to check: prices set on revenue or 'concept and hope'; people quitting day jobs to trade; money-losing firms funded by rising equity; transformative technology assumed to mean investor profits.

Sources:
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/docs/default-source/memos/2000-01-02-bubble.pdf
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/taking-the-temperature

body:
1. **What the market already knows.** 15 analysts asked questions on the Q2 FY26 call `[CC-Q2FY26]`. Their topics, in order of frequency:
   - (a) comp durability and difficult comparisons (Lasser, Ciccarelli, Grom, Cattel);
   - (b) how marketing and product split the drivers of the top line (Koenig, Bellinger, McShane);
   - (c) what to do with the ~$170M of tariff refunds (Owens, Ma);
   - (d) the gross-margin bridge: fuel, shrink and tariffs (Kelly, Hamblin);
   - (e) new-store productivity (Boss), the Five Beyond reset cost (Feldman), and store layout (Heinbockle).
   - **Nobody asked about** (i) the split between direct imports and domestic vendors, and what happens to tariffs embedded in the *domestic-vendor* 60% (§4.3); (ii) occupancy per sq ft on the new leases (§4.4); (iii) whether the "$2M / $0.4M / ~1-year payback" model still matches capex per store (§3.3).
2. **The variable that would change value most if we knew it better than consensus.** **Steady-state store-level margin after the tariff cycle and the pricing reset.** It has three parts. (i) Merchandise margin net of tariffs and vendor pass-through. (ii) Whether traffic-led comps of +14–23% are a level shift or a cohort/trend spike; consensus debates this. (iii) Real new-store returns against the company's undefined "payback". Almost nobody models (iii).
3. **The layers most likely to reveal it.**
   - L3: 10-K store-model text, capex guidance and pre-opening cost.
   - L4: the 10-K lease note, the 10-K/10-Q non-GAAP reconciliations, and the sourcing paragraph.
   - L6: a fixed price basket and price-point counts in three stores.

For a US specialty retailer with no controlling shareholder, the money-to-the-parent question (L16) becomes **"what does the company define for itself, and what does it leave out"**. KPI definitions do the work that related-party notes did in India.
